atoms.text: Delivered technical instruction to 800+ undergraduate students across Java and C++ development, database systems, advanced web technologies (Python), and advanced Oracle SQL — 3–4 lab sessions a week for cohorts averaging 80 — adapting explanations and one-to-one consultations to widely varying technical backgrounds
Authored troubleshooting documentation and standardised environment setup guides, cutting configuration time from 2+ hours to 30 minutes per student and reducing staff escalations by 90%

Kept labs unblocked by debugging the teaching materials themselves: found defects in the provided lab sheets — phpMyAdmin database configuration, broken JavaScript, mis-wired HTML/CSS references, a Python version mismatch in Advanced Web Technologies — and reported each to the module lecturer with the exact correction required — around 8 across the modules I supported, most in Web Technologies; all were blocking, so fast turnaround kept cohorts on schedule

Coordinated session cover and complex-issue triage with the TA team, proposed TAs to module leaders for modules matching their strengths, and brought mid-term joiners up to speed on session format, cohort progress, and known constraints

Automated manual billing and onboarding with Stripe subscription management and Google OAuth 2.0 (Next.js, Node.js/Express, MongoDB), cutting user onboarding time by over 80% while keeping the data pipeline GDPR-compliant

Built the admin console — drag-and-drop newsletter builder (5–6 sends/month), audience segmentation, RBAC user management — backed by Redis caching, Prometheus monitoring, Jenkins CI/CD, and 85%+ test coverage

Owned production security and reliability: TLS, input sanitisation, XSS/injection prevention, and rate limiting; diagnosed and resolved a critical SSL/DNS failure affecting mobile-network traffic, maintaining 99.9% average uptime across the engagement

Migrated payment handling from manually-tracked scheduled invoicing to Stripe as the sole payment processor, removing card and payment data from internal databases entirely and reducing PCI DSS compliance scope to Stripe's hosted flow

atoms.entity: Post-Quantum and Hybrid Signature Benchmarking in Cloud File-Signing Workflows
atoms.text: Executed 63,000+ benchmark runs across 7 signature schemes, 3 hash algorithms, and 5 payload sizes, with seeded randomisation, warm-up runs, and bootstrap confidence intervals

atoms.entity: Post-Quantum and Hybrid Signature Benchmarking in Cloud File-Signing Workflows
atoms.text: Showed FN-DSA matches classical ECDSA on signing (~0.4 ms) with the fastest verification in the suite (0.25 ms), while SLH-DSA costs ~1,600 ms per signature; quantified storage amplification — ML-DSA's 3.3 KB signatures add ~200 TB over five years for a 1-billion-record/month log pipeline — as the dominant migration cost, not compute

atoms.entity: Post-Quantum and Hybrid Signature Benchmarking in Cloud File-Signing Workflows

atoms.entity: Re:Link — Privacy-Preserving Peer-to-Peer Remote Access System
atoms.text: Designed a blind rendezvous protocol with full client-side end-to-end encryption (AES-256-GCM); the signalling server handles only ephemeral, encrypted state, enforcing a "nothing stored, nothing to steal" model

atoms.entity: Re:Link — Privacy-Preserving Peer-to-Peer Remote Access System
atoms.text: Implemented three-key derivation (k_sig, k_mac, sas) via HMAC-SHA256, delivering the root secret through the URL fragment so it never reaches the server; short-authentication-string verification mitigates man-in-the-middle attacks on the signalling channel

atoms.entity: Re:Link — Privacy-Preserving Peer-to-Peer Remote Access System
